results.title: Families of maps supported on a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ and $T$ be topological spaces and $P$ a set. A family of maps $f : P \times X \to T$ is supported on a set $S \subseteq X$ when it does not depend on the parameter outside $S$: $f(p, x) = f(p', x)$ for all $p, p' \in P$ and all $x \notin S$.

results.title: Adapted families of maps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ and $T$ be topological spaces, $P$ a set, $U = (U_\alpha)_{\alpha \in \iota}$ a family of subsets of $X$ and $k$ a natural number. A family of maps $f : P \times X \to T$ is adapted to $U$ with bound $k$ when there is a finite set $A$ of at most $k$ indices such that $f$ is supported on $\bigcup_{\alpha \in A} U_\alpha$.

results.title: Convex linear polyhedra
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ is a convex linear polyhedron when it is the convex hull of a finite set of points (equivalently, a bounded intersection of finitely many closed half-spaces).

results.title: Polyhedral subdivisions
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A polyhedral subdivision of a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ is a geometric simplicial complex in $\mathbb{R}^k$ with finitely many faces whose underlying space equals $P$.

results.title: Closed cells
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ and let $D \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ be a finite set (typically the vertex set of a face of a subdivision of $P$). The closed cell of $D$ in $P$ is the set of points of $P$ that lie in the convex hull of $D$, viewed as a subset of $P$.

results.title: Boundary subpolyhedra
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$. A subset $Q \subseteq P$ is a boundary subpolyhedron of $P$ when $Q$ is the convex hull of a finite set of points of $\mathbb{R}^k$, $Q$ lies in the intrinsic frontier (relative boundary) of $P$, and $Q$ is a face of $P$: whenever a point of $Q$ lies in the open segment between two points of $P$, both of those points lie in $Q$.

results.title: Essential isolated singularity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has an essential isolated singularity at $c \in \mathbb{C}$ when $f$ is holomorphic on some punctured disc $0 < |z - c| < r$ with $r > 0$, $f(z)$ has no finite limit as $z \to c$ with $z \ne c$, and $|f(z)|$ does not tend to $\infty$ as $z \to c$ with $z \ne c$.

results.title: Great Picard theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Suppose $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has an essential isolated singularity at $c \in \mathbb{C}$. Then there is at most one $w \in \mathbb{C}$ for which some $r > 0$ makes the set $\{z : 0 < |z - c| < r,\ f(z) = w\}$ finite; that is, with at most one exception, $f$ takes every complex value infinitely often on every punctured disc around $c$.

results.title: Convex measure
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Base of a measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $X$. A class $B$ of subsets of $X$ is a base of $\mu$ if every set in $B$ is measurable, $B$ is stochastically independent with respect to $\mu$, and every measurable set $A \subseteq X$ agrees up to a null set with a set $C$ in the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $B$, that is, $\mu(A \triangle C) = 0$.

results.title: Szpilrajn's Problem 191 has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The claim of Szpilrajn's Problem 191 is false: not every convex measure possesses a base. That is, there are a measurable space $X$ and a convex measure $\mu$ on $X$ such that no class of subsets of $X$ is a base of $\mu$.

results.title: Ewens sampling formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Ewens sampling formula: the probability, under the neutral infinite-alleles model with scaled mutation rate `θ = 4Nu`, that a sample of `n` genes has allelic partition `π` (`π.parts.count j` alleles carried by exactly `j` genes each): `n! * (∏ j, (θ / j) ^ (a j) / (a j)!) / θ^{(n)}` (Ewens 1972), for `θ > 0`.

results.title: The Ewens sampling formula is a probability distribution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Ewens sampling formula is a probability distribution on the partitions of `n` (Ewens 1972; equivalently, Cauchy's cycle-type formula `∑_{σ ∈ S_n} θ^{#cycles σ} = θ^{(n)}`).

results.title: Nonnegativity of the Ewens sampling formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Ewens sampling formula is nonnegative for `θ > 0`; with `sum_ewensProb` it is a probability distribution on the partitions of `n`.

results.title: Expected number of alleles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Expected number of alleles in a sample of `n` genes under the Ewens sampling formula: `E[K_n] = ∑_{i < n} θ / (θ + i)` (Ewens 1972).

results.title: One step of Hoppe's urn
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One step of Hoppe's urn on allelic partitions (Hoppe 1984): from a partition `π` of `k`, the next gene carries a new allele with probability `θ / (θ + k)` (target parts `1 ::ₘ π.parts`), and copies an allele carried by `j` genes with probability `j * a j / (θ + k)`, where `a j = π.parts.count j` (target parts `(j + 1) ::ₘ π.parts.erase j`). The value is the transition probability from `π` to `π'`.

results.title: Law of the allelic partition from Hoppe's urn
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The law of the allelic partition after `n` draws from Hoppe's urn, started from the empty sample: `hoppeLaw θ (n + 1) π' = ∑ π, hoppeLaw θ n π * hoppeStep θ π π'`.

results.title: Hoppe urn transition probabilities are nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Hoppe-urn transition probabilities are nonnegative.

results.title: Hoppe urn transition is stochastic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Hoppe-urn transition is stochastic: from every partition of `k` the probabilities of the partitions of `k + 1` sum to one.

results.title: Hoppe's urn generates the Ewens sampling formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Hoppe's urn generates the Ewens sampling formula (Hoppe 1984): after `n` draws, the allelic partition has law `ewensProb θ`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the Hoppe urn law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The law of Hoppe's urn after `n` draws is nonnegative for `θ > 0`.

results.title: Seating a customer at a new table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Seat customer `n` at a new table: the partition of `Fin (n + 1)` whose blocks are the blocks of `π` (relabeled into `Fin (n + 1)`) together with the singleton `{n}`.

results.title: Seating a customer at an occupied table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Seat customer `n` at the occupied table `B` of `π`: the block `B` becomes `B ∪ {n}` and the other blocks are unchanged.

results.title: Blocks of the partition after opening a new table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The blocks of `newTable π`.

results.title: Blocks of the partition after joining a table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The blocks of `joinTable π B hB`.

results.title: Seating a customer by a seating choice
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Seat customer `n` according to the choice `c`: `none` opens a new table, `some B` joins the occupied table `B`.

results.title: Seating probabilities in the Chinese restaurant process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The probability of each seating choice for customer `n` given the partition `π` of the first `n` customers: `θ / (n + θ)` for a new table, `|B| / (n + θ)` for the table `B`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of seating probabilities
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The seating probabilities are nonnegative for `θ > 0`.

results.title: Seating probabilities sum to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The seating probabilities sum to one for `θ > 0`.

results.title: Seating choice distribution of a customer
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The seating choice of customer `n`, as a probability distribution.

results.title: One step of the Chinese restaurant process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One step of the Chinese restaurant process: the law of the partition of `Fin (n + 1)` given the partition `π` of the first `n` customers.

results.title: Chinese restaurant process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Chinese restaurant process with parameter `θ > 0`: the law of the random partition of the customers `Fin n` into tables, built one customer at a time by `crpStep` (Aldous 1985, §11; Pitman 2006, ch. 3).

results.title: Closed-form law of the Chinese restaurant process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The closed-form law of the Chinese restaurant process, `θ^{|π|} ∏_{B ∈ π} (|B| - 1)! / θ^{(n)}` (Pitman 2006, §3.1). Every block is nonempty, so `|B| - 1` is never a truncated natural subtraction.

results.title: Removing the last customer undoes a seating
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Removing the last customer undoes every seating: restricting `seat π c` to the first `n` customers gives back `π`.

results.title: Injectivity of seating
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Different seating choices give different partitions.

results.title: Every partition arises from seating the last customer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every partition of `Fin (n + 1)` arises by seating customer `n` into its restriction to the first `n` customers.

results.title: Seating multiplies the closed-form law by the seating probability
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: One seating multiplies the closed-form law by the seating probability.

results.title: Law of the Chinese restaurant process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Law of the Chinese restaurant process (Pitman 2006, §3.1): `P(π) = θ^{|π|} ∏_{B ∈ π} (|B| - 1)! / θ^{(n)}`.

results.title: Chinese restaurant process law as a real number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The law of the Chinese restaurant process as a real number.

results.title: Exchangeability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Exchangeability, pointwise: relabeling the customers by a permutation `σ` does not change the probability of a partition.

results.title: Exchangeability of the Chinese restaurant process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Exchangeability of the Chinese restaurant process (Aldous 1985, §11): the law of the partition relabeled by any permutation of the customers is the law of the partition.

results.title: Consistency of the Chinese restaurant process
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Restricting the random partition of `Fin (n + 1)` to the first `n` customers gives the process with `n` customers.

results.title: Consistency for every sample size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Restricting the random partition of `Fin n` to the first `m ≤ n` customers gives the process with `m` customers.

results.title: Allelic partition of a set partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The allelic partition of a set partition of `Fin n`: the multiset of its block sizes, a partition of the integer `n`.

results.title: The block sizes follow Hoppe's urn
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The law of the multiset of block sizes after `n` customers is the law `Ewens.hoppeLaw` of Hoppe's urn on allelic partitions after `n` draws.

results.title: The allelic partition of the Chinese restaurant process follows the Ewens sampling formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The allelic partition of the Chinese restaurant process follows the Ewens sampling formula (Ewens 1972; Hoppe 1984): the multiset of block sizes after `n` customers has law `Ewens.ewensProb θ`.

results.title: Expected number of tables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Expected number of tables (expected number of alleles in a sample of `n` genes, Ewens 1972): `E[|π|] = ∑_{i < n} θ / (θ + i)`.
